source: ASME B16.5-2025, the 'Templates for Drilling' tables 7, 10, 13, 15, 17, 19 and 21 (SI units), transcribed from a purchased copy. The document itself is NOT in this repository; see standards-source/README.md.
note:
What ONE flanged joint needs. This pack exists to answer a single question: has enough bolting been taken off? The user's rule is that bolting is ordered in its own right, with an allowance over the calculated need, so nothing here derives an MTO line. It only supplies the floor that a take-off must clear. Bolt count and diameter are fixed by B16.5 and are safe to assert. LENGTH IS NOT: it depends on facing, gasket thickness and whether the joint is a stud or a machine bolt, so minLengthMm is the shortest credible raised-face stud with a spiral wound gasket and is marked unverified. A take-off shorter than that is wrong; one longer than it is a judgement this system does not second-guess.

THE TABLES USE TWO DIFFERENT COLUMN LAYOUTS. At Class 150 and 300 the last three columns are stud Raised Face, stud Ring Joint, and MACHINE BOLT Raised Face. From Class 400 up there is no machine bolt at all and the three columns are stud Raised Face, stud Male-and-Female / Tongue-and-Groove, and stud Ring Joint. Reading one layout with the other's column names silently files ring-joint lengths as machine-bolt lengths.

conventions.twoNutsPerStud: A stud bolt takes two nuts, one each end. A machine bolt takes one. nutsPerBolt is carried per joint because the ratio is a property of the fastener style, not of the flange.
conventions.oneJointTwoFlanges: A flanged joint is TWO flanges and ONE set of bolts. A take-off that counts a bolt set per flange doubles the order. The reconciler therefore works in joints, and how flange count becomes joint count is the caller's problem - it is stated, never guessed.
conventions.lengthUnverified: Every minLengthMm carries verified:false for the reason in the note. Do not quote one to a vendor.
conventions.studVersusMachineBolt: A stud bolt is a headless threaded rod with a nut at EACH end; a machine bolt has an integral hex head and takes ONE nut. That is why nutsPerBolt is not a free parameter - it follows from the fastener style, and the caller states the style rather than the ratio. B16.5 permits machine bolts only at Class 150 and Class 300, with raised or flat face; from Class 600 upward, and for any ring joint face, the joint must be studded. minLengthMachineBoltMm is therefore ABSENT above 300# - absent meaning not permitted, not unknown.
conventions.boltLengthIsMeasuredDifferently: A stud bolt length is measured first thread to last thread, EXCLUDING the end chamfers (the B18.31.2 'LEP' convention); a machine bolt is measured from UNDER THE HEAD. The two numbers are not comparable, which is why they are separate columns rather than one figure with a tolerance. A vendor quoting overall length including the points is roughly two thread pitches longer than the order, and that argument surfaces at incoming inspection.
conventions.seriesIsDimensionalOnly: Series A and B differ in bolt count, bolt diameter and bolt circle, so the series axis is REQUIRED here. It is deliberately absent from flange-pt-ratings, because the two series share identical pressure-temperature ratings. ADR-008 section 11.15.
conventions.absenceIsNotSufficiency: A size with no row is UNKNOWN, not adequate. Before this pack declared its coverage, a lookup above NPS 24 returned null and every caller read it as nothing to check. ADR-008 section 11.14.

coverage.note: Classes 150 through 2500, NPS 1/2 to 24, verified 2026-09-24. Class 400 below NPS 4 and Class 900 below NPS 3 have no dimensions of their own: the standard defers them to Class 600 and Class 1500, and those rows carry deferredToClass instead of numbers.

Tables 32-42, NPS 26-60, verified 2026-09-24. Series B stops at NPS 36 in Classes 400, 600 and 900; Series A Class 900 stops at NPS 48. Those sizes carry notOffered, which is not the same as untranscribed. A ring-joint stud length exists in Series A only, and only NPS 26-36.

sizesBeyondPipeSizesPack.reason: ASME B16.47-2025 dimensions flanges up to NPS 60. The pipe-sizes pack stops at NPS 48 because its own source, ASME B36.10M, has not been purchased, and no size may be invented from memory. These bolting rows are therefore transcribed and correct but not yet reachable: no line can be drawn at these sizes until B36.10M is bought and pipe-sizes extended. B16.47 itself prints no DN equivalent for them, so it cannot supply the gap.
